clue.text: See you in Rome — that's worth cutting university

indicators.note: cutting here means removing a piece from the word for worth

parts.note: worth means value

explanation.surface: Someone bids farewell in Rome, adding that the trip was worth leaving their studies for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' takes U out of VALUE. 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin farewell, as a Roman would say goodbye, is the word used here.

clue.text: William was a top performer, not born unlucky

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the letter for born from what precedes

parts.note: Bill is a short form of William
starred means was the leading performer

explanation.surface: A biography of a William who was a star from birth, yet ended unlucky.
explanation.walkthrough: BILL + STARRED gives BILLSTARRED; 'not born' removes the B.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-starred is a synonym for unlucky, as if born under bad stars.

clue.text: Day on board lagoon working boat

indicators.note: on board means taken inside the other letters, as a passenger in a vessel
working signals that the letters of lagoon are reworked

explanation.surface: A day spent aboard a boat working on the Venetian lagoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' turns LAGOON into GONOLA, and 'on board' puts D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondola is a type of boat, the Venetian rowing craft.

clue.text: Retired faced pressure in a lot of work performed quickly

indicators.note: retired, as in withdrew, signals a backward movement of the whole assembly
in places one piece inside the other
a lot of means most of, dropping the last letter

parts.note: an opus is a work, especially of music
faced means met
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A retiree met with pressure while doing a lot of work at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims OPUS to OPU; 'in' puts METP inside, giving OPMETPU; 'Retired' turns the whole thing backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Music described as uptempo is played at a fast pace.

clue.text: Contest in which all runners finish tied

definitions.text: Contest in which all runners finish tied

parts.words: Contest in which all runners finish tied
parts.note: seems to describe a dead heat, but the runners are literally tied together by the legs in pairs

explanation.surface: A race where every competitor crosses the line at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A school sports-day race run in pairs with one leg of each bound together.

clue.text: Where one might spot a criminal band before judge

definitions.text: Where one might spot a criminal

parts.note: a line is a band or stripe
to be up is to appear before a judge in court

explanation.surface: A witness picks out an offender, and a gang awaits trial.
explanation.walkthrough: An identity parade, where a witness picks out a suspect, is called a line-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Police use an identity parade so a witness can point out the suspect.

clue.text: Whale needs power, alternatively graceful bearing

parts.note: or expresses an alternative
poise is graceful bearing

explanation.surface: A whale needs strength or else elegance as it moves.
explanation.definitionFit: A porpoise is a small toothed cetacean, loosely called a whale.

clue.text: Charge added to complimentary sponge

indicators.note: added to places the charge after the other word

parts.note: complimentary means free of charge
a load is a charge, as of a gun or a burden

explanation.surface: A fee added to something meant to be complimentary, like a bath sponge.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponge is to live off others, which is to freeload.

clue.text: Brewer's using this possibly to exploit books about English

indicators.note: about means going around, so the other words enclose the letter for English

parts.note: to tap is to exploit a resource
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A beer brewer exploits volumes about England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means the pair encloses the E. 'to' is a link; the brewer is one brewing tea, not beer, and the definition leans on the rest of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone brewing tea would likely be using a pot made for it.

clue.text: Turner working on water reproduced rices and weeds with charm

indicators.note: reproduced suggests the letters are produced again in a new order

explanation.surface: A water-driven turner grows rice and weeds, as if by magic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reproduced' rearranges RICES, WEEDS and CHARM; 'and' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient device is a rotating helix inside a tube that lifts water.

clue.text: Copper leads anger about Conservative partitioned area

indicators.note: leads means comes in front of the rest

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: about means the word for anger surrounds the letter for Conservative

parts.note: bile means anger or bad temper

explanation.surface: A policeman heads up angry protest about a Tory, in a divided room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets the anger round the Conservative and 'leads' puts the metal first. 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: A small screened-off compartment, as in an office or toilet block.

clue.text: Hoax challenge mostly overcome

parts.note: a con is a hoax or swindle

indicators.note: mostly drops the final letter of the word

parts.note: to query is to challenge

explanation.surface: A hoax that challenges and nearly beats someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To conquer is to defeat or overcome.

clue.text: Need priest working to ordain in advance

indicators.note: working signals the letters are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A busy priest is required to ordain someone ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: To predestine is to fate or decree beforehand.

clue.text: Straight man paid for professional services

definitions.meaning: the comedian's stooge who sets up the punchlines
having been paid a professional's charge

explanation.definitionFit: A comic's stooge is called this, and the past participle of the verb for charging a fee is identical.

clue.text: Like a salad? Fetch in meat!

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: veal is a meat
to get is to fetch

explanation.surface: A diner asks whether the salad is coming and demands meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the verb inside the meat; the question mark flags that the definition is an example of plant matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Vegetal means relating to plants, which a salad is made of.

clue.text: Large working historic barn projected to last a good while

definitions.text: projected to last a good while

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is on
a grange was historically a barn or granary

explanation.surface: A big old barn being restored is expected to stand for years.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-range forecast is one covering a long time ahead.

clue.text: Dull London market with no room for meetings

indicators.note: with no tells us to remove the room from the market's name

parts.note: Leadenhall Market is a covered market in the City of London
a hall is a room for meetings

explanation.surface: A London market without a meeting room is a dreary place.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaden, heavy like lead, means dull and lifeless.

clue.text: Fish is rock mostly sliced with egg on

indicators.note: sliced with means cut open and filled with the other piece
mostly drops the final letter

parts.note: stone is rock
to egg on is to urge

explanation.surface: A fish dish of sliced rock, served with an egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts STONE to STON, and 'sliced with' opens it for URGE: ST(URGE)ON. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is a large fish, source of caviar.

clue.text: What lifts iron worker chasing a new surge

indicators.note: chasing means following behind the other pieces

parts.note: a tide is a surge
to press is to iron clothes
an ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: An ironworker runs after a sudden surge.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a drug lifts the mood of someone who is depressed.

clue.text: Runs to the front in shadow dance

indicators.note: to the front moves that letter to the start of the word

parts.note: an umbra is a shadow
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone runs forward in a shadowy dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The R of UMBRA goes to the front, giving the Cuban dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Latin ballroom dance.

clue.text: Ice does hurt a pastoral area

indicators.note: hurt suggests the letters are damaged into a new shape

explanation.surface: Icy weather harms a rural farming district.
explanation.definitionFit: A diocese is a bishop's district, over which pastoral care is exercised.

clue.text: Arrive having eaten with band and return to start again

parts.note: to come is to arrive
full means having eaten enough
a circle is a band or ring

explanation.surface: Someone arrives after a meal with a musical band and goes back to the beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to end up back where one began.

clue.text: Pester military policeman during routine working

indicators.note: during places the policeman inside the other letters
working signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A military policeman nags during a routine shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges the routine into IORTUNE, and 'during' puts the policeman inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To importune is to pester with repeated requests.

clue.text: Concrete around a small window

indicators.note: around means the first word encloses the others

parts.note: cement is a binding material for concrete

explanation.surface: Builders pour concrete around a small window frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A casement is a hinged window.

clue.text: Act up in agitation characteristic of the working class?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a flap is a state of agitation

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading upwards, so the letters go backwards

explanation.surface: A worker acts up angrily in a class protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the act round into TCA, and 'in' puts that inside the agitation. 'agitation' looks like an anagram signal but is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The cloth cap is stereotypically worn by working-class men in Britain.

clue.text: Draw eastern crimson rose so very high

parts.note: to tow is to draw or pull
crimson is a shade of red

explanation.surface: A painter draws an eastern crimson rose that grew very tall.
explanation.definitionFit: Towered means loomed or rose to a great height.

clue.text: Warning for shipping company involved in Lima, perhaps

indicators.note: involved in places the company inside the other word

parts.note: the lima is a kind of bean

explanation.surface: A shipping company warning involving the Peruvian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Lima looks like the capital of Peru, but is the bean.
explanation.definitionFit: A beacon is a signal light warning ships.

clue.text: Message from taxi learner acquiring knowledge finally

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
L is the abbreviation for learner, as on L-plates

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A taxi-driving learner gets a message about the Knowledge test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acquiring' is a link. The Knowledge is London cabbies' test of street routes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable is a telegram, a message.
